messages.subject: drop in facet_grid and facet_wrap (Plot Builder)
messages.subject_clean: drop in facet_grid and facet_wrap (Plot Builder)
messages.body_plain:
Hi all, I have detected a bug and got a feature request regarding to the facet elements of the Plot Builder. They are related to the issue of keeping/dropping levels of factors that was already discussed some months ago:
https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/deducer/a4y8xOoz6Bo

Both facet_grid and facet_wrap admit the argument "drop", to define whether the "unused" levels of the chosen factors should be ignored, or printed in empty facets.
http://docs.ggplot2.org/current/facet_grid.html
http://docs.ggplot2.org/0.9.3.1/facet_wrap.html

The Plot Builder provides a "drop" checkbox for facet_wrap. But when it is unckecked, the argument that is set to FALSE is "as.table", not "drop".

In the case of facet_grid there is no such checkbox. That's not a bug of course, just an "absent feature", but I think that it would be nice to have it there too.

Best regards,
Helios

messages.subject: Issue when trying to run EcosimR
messages.subject_clean: Issue when trying to run EcosimR
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I am trying the new R version of the famous null model generator Ecosim by Gotelli.
This is being ported over to R as EcoSimR.

It runs in a native 32 bit R window but not under Jaguar/Deducer.
At least the first part I have tried does not plot and indicates an error.

> Null.Result <- Null.Model.Engine(Param.List)
>
> Output.Results(Param.List,Null.Result)
Error in plot.new <http://plot.new>() : figure margins too large

How to tweak this?

Code for plotting routine is below and is not linked to ggplot.
+++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
Null.Model.Plot <- function (Null.Model.Out=list(Obs=runif(1),Sim=runif(n=1000)),Date.Stamp=date())

{

  opar <- par(no.readonly=TRUE)
  par(cex=1, cex.axis = 1.5,
      cex.main=1,cex.lab=1.6)
  par (mar=c(5,6,4,2)+0.1)
  #------------------------------------------------------
  hist(Null.Model.Out$Sim, breaks=20, col="royalblue3",

       xlab="Simulated Metric",ylab="Frequency",main="",
       xlim=range(c(Null.Model.Out$Sim,Null.Model.Out$Obs)))
  abline(v=Null.Model.Out$Obs,col="red",lty="solid",lwd=2.5)
  abline(v=quantile(Null.Model.Out$Sim,c(0.05,0.95)),col="black",lty="dashed",lwd=2.5)
  abline(v=quantile(Null.Model.Out$Sim,c(0.025,0.975)),col="black",lty="dotted",lwd=2.5)
  mtext(as.character(Date.Stamp),side=3,adj=1,line=3)

}
##########################################################################################
## Niche.Overlap.Plot function
## Function for plotting observed and simulated utilization matrix
## Takes as input an input data matrix, a randomization algorithm, and the time stamp
##
##

Niche.Overlap.Plot <- function (Data=matrix(rpois(80,1),nrow=5), Algorithm="RA3", Date.Stamp=date(), Plot.Output="screen")
{

opar<- par(no.readonly=TRUE)
if (Plot.Output == "file") par(mfrow=c(2,1))
Data <- Data/rowSums(Data)
plot(rep(1:ncol(Data),times = nrow(Data)),
     rep(1:nrow(Data),each=ncol(Data)),
     xlab="Resource Category",ylab="Species",cex=10*sqrt(t(Data)/pi),col="red",lwd=2,
     main="Observed Utilization Matrix",col.main="red",cex.main=1.5)
if (Plot.Output=="file") mtext(as.character(Date.Stamp),side=3,adj=1,line=3)

Fun.Alg <- get(Algorithm)
One.Null.Matrix <- Fun.Alg(Data)
One.Null.Matrix <- One.Null.Matrix/rowSums(One.Null.Matrix)
plot(rep(1:ncol(One.Null.Matrix),times = nrow(One.Null.Matrix)),
     rep(1:nrow(One.Null.Matrix),each=ncol(One.Null.Matrix)),
     xlab="Resource Category",ylab="Species",cex=10*sqrt(t(One.Null.Matrix)/pi),col="royalblue3",lwd=2,
     main="Simulated Utilization Matrix",col.main="royalblue3",cex.main=1.5)
par(opar)
}
++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
Nick Gotelli uses R Commander for his GUI but I would prefer to stick with Deducer if possible.

Before I run real data I want to make sure this is working with the sample MacArthur warbler data set.

Bruce

messages.body_plain:
Hi again all,
Apparently needed more caffeine in my system this morning.

Buried in the user files I did find this issue was addressed and resolved.

If the program did not run successfully, the most likely error message
you might have received in
the console window is:

Error in plot.new <http://plot.new>() : figure margins too large

If this happens, the plotting window is too small to accommodate the
graphic. Either re-size the plot
window, or change the default setting for the Plot.Output option from
screen to file. With this
change, the graphics output will be sent to two pdf files that can be
opened separately.

So by dragging the device Java GD (2) to a wider size on screen it now
plots.
I would prefer to use faceting and try also changing the geomes but have
yet to determine where the plot data used will be so I can open Plot
Builder.

Bruce

change the Type for time form Factor to time it deletes all the values
in this data field from the data table.

I want to do density plots with density on Y axis and time on X axis.
Alas seems I am not the sharpest Crayola in the box this morning and
seem not to be able to get this one working.

The end goal is to stack multiple plots (which works very nicely in Plot
Builder) and color by species to visually look at night time activity
patterns for comparison among them all.

Seems that this should be straight forward to have times on the X axis
in plot builder.

Bruce

messages.subject: Re: Query on plotting times
messages.subject_clean: Query on plotting times
messages.body_plain:
Bruce,

To convert the dates, open the data viewer in variable view. in type, select Date. A dialog will pop-up with date formats, click other. enter %m%d%y and click okay. Your dates should be converted.

If you don't get a pop-up make sure your Deducer is updated.

If you want to include your times, change your csv to have one column with both the data and hour. Preferably in a common format like: yyyy-mm-dd hh:mm:ss

Then do the same process you did for date, but selecting time and the appropriate datetime format in the pop-up.

ian
